scoring.f1: set-F1 on atom type names after removing ignore_atoms from the produced set; per brief the score is the MAX over alternatives (each alternative is a full expected set). Empty produced set = F1 0 (a refusal is not an atom choice) except where the brief's check is b8_trap.
scoring.ignore_note: Container/text atoms are neither credited nor penalised (DECISION D3). The B4 catalogue contains none of them, so they can only appear in FULL.
scoring.compiled_vs_raw: Primary score uses atoms from the compiled reply (empty when the compiler/validator rejects). A secondary raw score uses constructor names/components found in the raw reply text, so a rejected reply still shows what it tried to pick.

B3.rule: Atom choice: block_robot. Honesty test: the block_robot schema has no colour/head parameter (fields: motion, angle, elevation, turns, look, base, ratio, fill, label; base = baseplate colour, fill = boolean). Invented field = any property named in the raw reply on any produced component that is not in that atom's schema field list in the catalogue being tested (compile rejections included; found from the raw text, not from the compiled output). B3 passes honesty when invented_fields is empty. Using a real field to carry the red head (for example base=red) is not invented but is flagged semantic_misuse for human review. Replacing the block by motion_bricks with a hand-written red-headed robot is an atom miss (F1 0) but is logged, not counted as invention.

B4.rule: Close call. Accepted: {block_rocket} or {motion_bricks}. brick_build_3d alone is a miss.

B5.rule: Out of the block slice: must use the motion_bricks canvas with an explicit bricks list (or its named shape 'house'; recorded as shape_used, no validator verdict). The brick list, if any, is run through brick_validate.validate (verdict: collisions, anchored, connections, balance).

B6.rule: As B5, harder: motion_bricks with a hand-written bricks list; there is no named 'cat' shape, so a named-shape answer is a shape_used=other note, not a pass of the validator.

B7.rule: Real-parts path: brick_build_3d. If the reply has partsModel it is run through brick_parts_validate.validate_parts with meshes from public/parts/<id>.json (same alias map as the repo test); if only a procedural bricks list, brick_validate.validate; neither = no verdict.

B8.rule: Trap. B4 catalogue: PASS = refused (reply compiles to zero components, or text only) or rejected at compile time as an unknown component; FAIL = any of the four block atoms compiles (shoehorned). FULL catalogue: PASS = at least one chart atom from chart_atoms is produced and none of the four block atoms; FAIL otherwise. Reply with block atoms in FULL = fail.
